place.en: Surajgarh Haveli · the account room · Thursday, 9:15 AM

brief.en: Three people in this bazaar are paying somebody to stay quiet, and the demands arrive by pigeon — a sum, a place, a day, rolled inside a brass ring on a bird's leg. Each note knows a thing that is written down in exactly one room in Jaipur. The birds belong to Bansi, who flies them where he is told and cannot read a word of what he is carrying.

iraNote.en: “A pigeon is a postman who can’t be questioned. So question the paper instead — where it was torn from, and what ink it was written in.”

teaser.en: Three people are paying to stay quiet, and every demand arrives on a pigeon's leg.

text.en: “₹2,000 in the niche behind the Ganesh at the Chandpol baori. Thursday, before the second bell.” A clerk's hand, ruled paper.
Stamped SG-19. It is a Surajgarh loft ring, and the paper was rolled inside it, not tied to it.
₹9,000 short. The entry that closes the fortnight sits over an erasure, in the munshi's own hand.
Ruled, eleven lines to the inch, torn along a stitched edge. It is daybook paper, and this haveli buys it by the ream.
Three leaves cut out close to the stitching with a blade. The stubs are still in the binding, and they count three.
A pledged dowry, a written-off debt, and a settlement kept out of the family book. All three are recorded in the account room and nowhere else in Jaipur.
Iron-gall, and the same batch as the account room's own well — the estate buys it by the seer from one shop in Kishanpole.
The 4th, the 11th, the 18th. On each of those mornings the reading of the estate accounts moved one week closer.
A hawk's barred feather caught in the netting.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — a hawk over a pigeon loft is a Tuesday, and the netting is why the birds are still alive

text.en: Out of true by two rattis, in the shop's favour.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — she reported it to the guild herself in Asadh, which is not what a blackmailer does with a secret

text.en: All three payers are in it, with dates and sums.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — a moneylender lists everybody; that is the entire job description

text.en: Asks the munshi to lay the Teej accounts before her.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — she asks in the same month every year, and the reply is what he is frightened of

text.en: Madhav bought ghee at the Chandpol market on all three of the drop mornings.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — he buys ghee at Chandpol four mornings a week and has since 1998

text.en: A boy in a red cap on the third step, close to the niche.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — the water-carrier's son, on those steps every morning of his life

text.en: “Munshi-ji gives me a bird and a rooftop and I let it go. I do not know what is in the ring. I could not know what is in the ring.”
“I have paid twice. What that note knew about my pledge, four people know — and three of them have been dead for years.”
“Nine thousand walked out of this room on Teej night and I wrote it closed to keep a name out of the bazaar. The reading is in Kartik. I have until Kartik to put it back.”

hook.en: keeps every book this family owns

confession.en: Cut three leaves from his own daybook, wrote three demands in the estate's ink, and sent them out on Bansi's birds — to put back nine thousand rupees he had covered for somebody else before the accounts are read in Kartik.

hook.en: every bird that flew is his

alibi.en: He flies a bird to a rooftop for whoever asks and cannot read a line of what he carries. A courier who cannot read the demand cannot have written it.

hook.en: assays half the pledges in Johari Bazaar

alibi.en: She is one of the three paying, and she brought the second note to the police herself rather than the money.

hook.en: knows what every house in this lane owes

alibi.en: He knows the debts but not the settlement kept out of the family book — that one never left the account room, and it is in all three notes.

hook.en: the haveli, the loft and the account room are all hers

alibi.en: She is the one person here who could simply ask for the money, and the accounts she has been demanding for a month are the very ones the notes are paying to hide.

hook.en: in every room of this house by six each morning

alibi.en: He was at Chandpol on all three mornings, which is where he is four mornings a week — and he signs his own wages with a thumb.

setting.en: The loft, forty birds settling, the netting throwing squares of shade.

ask.en: How does a bird know where to go?

answer.en: “It doesn't. It knows where home is. You carry it away and it comes back — that is the whole of it.”

note.en: So the notes did not fly *to* the payers. Somebody carried a bird out and let it come home with the reply.

ask.en: Who asks you for a bird?

answer.en: “Anybody in the house. They are the family's birds. I only keep them.”

note.en: Anybody in the house — which is the answer that makes the loft useless and the ring interesting.

ask.en: This ring is SG-19, off your own loft.

answer.en: “Munshi-ji gives me a bird and a rooftop and I let it go. I do not know what is in the ring. I could not know what is in the ring.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the brass ring. He will not be told about his own birds — put the number in his hand.

note.en: He says the name without a flicker, because to him it is not an accusation. It is who hands him the bird.

setting.en: The goldsmith's shop, the shutter half down, a second note still folded in her till.

answer.en: “Two thousand, twice. The third I brought to you instead, which is why we are talking.”

note.en: She stopped paying and came in. That is the one move a blackmailer cannot survive.

ask.en: What does the note have on you?

answer.en: “A pledge I took in and should not have. It is written in one book and I am not the one who wrote it.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the note itself. She will not name her own secret to somebody who has not read it.

note.en: Four people knew, three are dead, and the fourth keeps the book it is written in.

ask.en: Did you go to the baori?

answer.en: “Twice, before the second bell, and both times the niche was empty within the hour. I did not see a soul lift it.”

note.en: Empty within the hour, unwatched. Whoever collects knows exactly how long that step stays quiet.

setting.en: The upper courtyard, the account books she has asked for four times stacked unopened.

ask.en: Who may take a leaf from the daybook?

answer.en: “Nobody. It is stitched precisely so that nobody may.”

note.en: And three leaves are gone, cut close to the stitching by somebody who knew that.

ask.en: You have been asking for the Teej accounts since Bhadra.

answer.en: “Four times. I am told they are with the binder. A book is not at the binder for six weeks unless somebody wants it there.”

lockedHint.en: Pin her letter. She answers her own correspondence and very little else.

note.en: Six weeks at the binder. The reading is in Kartik, and somebody is counting the same weeks she is.

answer.en: “Every rupee is called out in front of the family. It has been done that way since my husband's grandfather.”

note.en: Called out in front of the family. A hole of nine thousand has a date on it.

setting.en: The account room, the inkwell open, the daybook shut under his hand.

ask.en: Three leaves are cut out of this daybook.

answer.en: “Spoiled pages. I cut them and I burn them; a spoiled page in a ledger is worse than no page.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the daybook. Counting stubs to a munshi is not the same as showing him the stubs.

note.en: Three spoiled pages, three notes. He does not ask how many notes there are.

ask.en: The notes are in this room's ink and this room's paper.

answer.en: “Half of Kishanpole sells that ink and every counting house in the city rules its paper the same.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the ink slip. He will argue the paper all morning; the batch is the thing he cannot spread across a city.

note.en: One shop, one batch, one seer at a time, bought against this estate's name.

ask.en: Nine thousand is missing from the Teej fortnight, and the entry that closes it is yours.

answer.en: “Nine thousand walked out of this room on Teej night and I wrote it closed to keep a name out of the bazaar. The reading is in Kartik. I have until Kartik to put it back.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the jama-kharch. He has answered everything else with a shrug; the erasure is in his own hand.

note.en: He covered for somebody, and then went out to the three people whose secrets he keeps to pay for the covering. He never once considered naming the man.

correction.en: A crooked assay scale is a guild matter. Nine thousand rupees that must be back in the book before the family hears it read out is the reason.
A moneylender's book lists everybody in the lane. Only one room in Jaipur holds all three of these secrets at once, and only one man holds that room.
A boy in a red cap on the baori steps is a boy on the steps. The demands went out on a bird flown by somebody who cannot read them — that is why no hand ever carried a note.

text.en: The note is on ruled paper torn along a stitched edge. Paper torn out of a book leaves stubs behind — go and find the book that is short by three.

bankedClue.en: A Surajgarh loft ring, SG-19 — three demands flown by a boy who cannot read them
